citeinfo.title: Critical mineral deposits of the United States (ver. 2.0, April 2024)

descript.abstract: This product includes GIS and data tables for 684 deposits in the United States and Puerto Rico that have past or present production or resources for critical minerals. Deposits are classified by mineral system and deposit types using the Earth Mineral Resources Initiative (EMRI) framework of Hofstra and Kreiner (2020) and the focus areas defined by Dicken and others (2022).
descript.purpose: The intent is for the GIS and table to show where the focus areas in Dicken and others (2022) have documented critical minerals from the USGS mineral occurrence databases (MRDS, USMIN, and ARDF).

srcinfo.srccontr: Each deposit in this database is associated with a focus area from this source.
MRDS records were queried for sites that produced critical minerals in the past or have resources for critical minerals reported.
USMIN records were queried for sites that produced critical minerals in the past or have resources for critical minerals reported.
ARDF records were queried for sites that produced critical minerals in the past or have resources for critical minerals reported.

procstep.procdesc:
USGS mineral occurrence databases MRDS, ARDF, and USMIN were queried for sites that produced critical minerals in the past or have resources for critical minerals reported by searching for sites that mention a critical mineral commodity. USGS Mineral Commodity Summary reports were examined for mention of active mines for critical mineral commodities. Critical minerals are those included on the 2022 U.S. critical minerals list. Data were also extracted from the data tables and references in the focus area compilation of Dicken and others (2022). In addition, mining company reports for properties in the U.S. were compiled along with information reported on company websites and in press releases. Site names, locations, and production and resource data were extracted from the source materials. The sites were plotted in the GIS of focus areas. Focus area names, mineral systems, and deposit types were related to each site. Duplicates were deleted along with any site that did not have either past production data reported or resource information reported. The most recent and reliable data were selected, such as data from technical reports that meet international reporting standards for resources and reserves. Sites that mention past, but unquantified production were deleted. Production and resource data are reported as noted in source documents (short tons, metric tons, pounds, and so forth).
2022 critical minerals list - https://www.usgs.gov/news/national-news-release/us-geological-survey-releases-2022-list-critical-minerals.
Full references for sources used can also be found in the associated stand-alone table under the tab called References.
